findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded in ApplicationController#set_locale
findings.body: Locale files are loaded lazily, and `translate` only calls `load_locale(config.locale)`. The new `ensure_loaded!` is called only from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any code that sets the locale elsewhere (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, `I18n.with_locale`, rake tasks, other entry points) will never load the site-default or `:en` fallback locales. A key missing in the user's locale will then still come back as 'translation missing' because the fallback backend finds nothing in the unloaded fallback locales. The loading should happen inside `translate` or `load_locale`, not just one controller filter.

findings.title: LRU cache key ignores the fallback chain
findings.body: The cached key is `key + config.locale + backend.object_id`. With the new fallback list, the result for a locale now depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`. If an admin changes the default locale, cached translations that were resolved through the old fallback (or cached as 'translation missing') stay stale until the cache is reset. The key or cache invalidation should account for the fallback chain, or the cache should be cleared when `default_locale` changes.

findings.title: ensure_loaded! mutates @loaded_locales outside the mutex
findings.body: `@loaded_locales ||= []` and the `include?` check run outside `LOAD_MUTEX`, while `load_locale` mutates the array under the mutex and `reload!` resets it to a new array. Concurrent requests can race with a reload, or read the array while another thread appends to it. The check is repeated inside `load_locale`, so the outer unsynchronized check and initialization are a thread-safety smell, and `@loaded_locales` is still nil if `load_locale` is called before `ensure_loaded!`.

findings.title: No tests for the new fallback behavior
findings.body: The PR replaces `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` (previously production-only) with a custom global fallback list that applies in every environment, including test and development. It adds no specs covering the fallback order (user locale, then site default, then en), the lazy loading of fallback locales, or the interaction with the translate cache. Behavior changes in all environments without any coverage.
